Recent findings suggest that 'I think that (Wenger's future) is a very pertinent question,' adds another ally. 'It's on his mind and it's a significant decision. To a much lesser degree, his age may well be a factor too. But he has the fire in his belly. He has energy. I know that.

In a recent development, 'He had a certain aim and certain targets when he started with FIFA. And he hasn't met them yet.'.

Under Wenger's stewardship and guidance, FIFA have established 60 academies in previously under-resourced football backwaters such as India, Uzbekistan and Fresh Caledonia.

'We provide the structure, the finance and – by way of top coaches – the expertise,' explains a source from the governing body. 'For example, we have Spanish coaches leading the way in India. We basically have coaches coaching the coaches, if that makes sense.

Sources indicate that 'Arsene believes every child in the world should have a pathway if they have the talent. India, for example, have never been to a senior men's World Cup. Arsene wants to change that.'.

In a recent development, at last month's Under-15 World Cup, 500 players were involved who had emerged from Wenger's FIFA academies. The governing body's stated aim is to have established 75 by the end of next year.

Sources indicate that 'In Arsene's mind, the number would actually be 100,' laughs his associate. 'And he knows he isn't there yet.'.

Spain, watched by Infantino (left), raise the Under-15 World Cup in Azerbaijan last month.

The Under-15 World Cup was one of Wenger's ideas and is an eight-a-side tournament with the emphasis on technique and quality.

Sources indicate that wenger is evangelical about it all. Some would – and do – say he remains a dreamer at heart. He also remains a small details person. For example, the reason he has established the Under-17 World Cup as an annual event is that he doesn't want a single talented footballer to fall through the cracks and miss out simply by being born a year too early or too late.

Industry observers note that the Frenchman is not, however, without his contradictions. Once asked privately how a father of a daughter could justify a FIFA decision to hold the 2034 World Cup in Saudi Arabia – where the women's rights problem remains deeply contentious – Wenger suggested that he wished only to 'effect change from within'.

In a recent development, just as pertinent is the impact Wenger has undoubtedly had – for better or for worse – on football's global calendar. You don't have to have a particularly sharp memory to recall the many times Wenger railed against the dangers of too much travel and playing-time on his top players when he was in charge at Arsenal.

According to recent reports, of all the top English clubs, Arsenal were the last to commit to arduous pre-season tours to places like America and the Far East and that was simply because Wenger was the manager. He always preferred a week in the Austrian mountains to a schlep round the world.

Now – eight-and-a-half years on from his departure from the Emirates – Wenger has been firmly attached to FIFA's gravy train for some time, a driving force behind the expanded summer Club World Cup and a key advocate of a proposal to hold the World Cup every two years that ultimately didn't get off the ground.

Wenger is on record on the matter. 'The welfare of the players in the last 20 years has increased dramatically,' Wenger has said. 'When you look at injury prevention, recovery work, nutrition and advances in medical technology. It is unrecognisable from what it used to be.

'Also VAR has helped with the protection of players, as players know they cannot escape from making bad tackles that cause injury.'.

Recent findings suggest that club coaches across Europe may raise eyebrows at that. So would many of those who opposed the expansion of this year's World Cup to 48 teams. But alternative theories are also in play.

Asked how a father of a daughter could justify the decision to hold the 2034 World Cup in Saudi Arabia – where women's rights are deeply contentious – Wenger noted he only wished to 'effect change from within'.

Many wanted Wenger to challenge Infantino's presidency, hoping it would serve to cleanse FIFA's reputation for sleaze.

'Arsene was seen as poster boy for the two-year World Cup and, yes, he put his weight behind it,' explains our FIFA source. 'But in truth we were being asked that question by some member associations. It was FIFA's duty to look into it.

According to recent reports, 'The mistake some people make is to look at everything from a European perspective. European football is blessed but not everybody is. Many countries just don't play as much competitive football and Arsene is strong on the global view.

'He listened to the pushback but wants to give opportunities to clubs from smaller nations in things like the Club World Cup and a bigger World Cup. It's not just about England, France, Germany, Argentina and Brazil.

It has been revealed that 'When you are a club manager you are paid to be essentially selfish and when he looks back he recognises that. His horizons have been broadened. Some of the smaller nations don't have the calendar congestion that exists in England, for example. His principles remain the same but he has just seen another perspective.'.

By his own self-effacing admission, Wenger has always led a rather monastic existence. Splitting his time between Zurich – where FIFA have their HQ – and his home in the north London enclave of Totteridge, he still endeavours to run 5km every morning. After that, it's football.

Industry observers note that 'If there is football on TV from one of the leagues then I will watch it,' he told Mo Farah on a recent episode of the Olympic Champion's podcast. 'It's simply what I like to do.'.

It is not too simplistic to say that the sport remains Wenger's obsession. It is hard to imagine him without it at the core of his life. Equally, it is difficult to imagine a return to club football in any meaningful capacity.

The wounds caused by what he felt was a rancorous departure from Arsenal have healed but that, nevertheless, remains a chapter closed.

'Arsene was seen as poster boy for the two-year World Cup and, yes, he put his weight behind it,' explains our FIFA source.

'Sir Alex Ferguson was capable of staying tight to Manchester United but for Arsene and Arsenal it was different'.

'It would be disingenuous to say it wasn't all a bit distant and uncomfortable for a while,' says a source with knowledge of the situation. 'Arsene made a decision to step away from it completely. Sir Alex Ferguson was capable of staying tight to Manchester United but for Arsene and Arsenal it was different.

'The ending was different for a start. So it was a bit like a divorce. You need some distance for a while before you can remember what you liked about each other back in the first place.

Sources indicate that 'But that's where it is now. It's thawed. There is semi-regular contact. He's been back to a game, even if it was just the one.'.

For Wenger, the pull of what he sees as unfinished business with FIFA may remain strong. Equally, beyond the rather waspish and phlegmatic public face has always run a river of steel.

'You don't go toe to toe with Fergie all of those years and have all that personal c**p poured on you by Jose Mourinho and come out the other side in one piece if you haven't got some proper b***s,' notes one of our sources.

'Some of us were surprised how long it took him to come out and speak publicly about his opposition to Infantino's World Cup sell-off. It was discussed. But he got there in the end. The bottom line is that he has his principles and he already has his relevance. Infantino constantly has to fight for his. Arsene does not. If he isn't comfortable where he works, he will always find something else.'.

Recent findings suggest that it's a view thoroughly endorsed by just about everybody in Wenger's orbit. 'Whatever he does next – whether with FIFA or somewhere else – it will be in football,' adds an ally. 'The next chapter will be his decision. He is very focused. And there is already a legacy.'.

Wenger and Infantino will in all likelihood be side by side in Doha next week as the second staging of FIFA's 48-team Under-17 World Cup gets into full swing.

Teams from Tanzania, Mozambique and Vietnam will make their debut in the 104-match tournament. In Qatar, FIFA will present a thoroughly united front with Wenger's avowed principles at its core.

Sources indicate that 'You can play with an orange or you can make a ball with paper,' Wenger told The Independent in a rare interview three years ago. 'That's why football is so popular. But today if you want to get to a good level of education in football, in some countries you don't get it.

'I find that not right because, in many countries, there are some private initiatives, but the parents have to pay to get the children in there and play. For me, it doesn't matter if you're rich or poor. If you are good, you come in.

'Our academies are free, just open to talent. You have to adapt and find a solution in every country.'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scegli FcInter1908 come tuo sito preferito su Google: clicca qui.

Stefano Vecchi, tecnico dell'Inter U23, ha parlato in sala stampa dopo il successo contro il Potenza: "Oggi per vincere abbiamo avuto bisogno di tutti. Questa è la vittoria del gruppo, di tutti: del portiere che ha fatto parate importanti, degli attaccanti, di chi è entrato e ha risolto la partita come Agbonifo. Come ho sempre detto è un gruppo di ragazzi che lavora sodo e bene, si fanno sempre trovare pronti, e contro un Potenza di questo tipo ce n'era bisogno. Quando si gioca tutti al massimo delle potenzialità, quest'anno siamo competitivi e stiamo bene in campo con tutti. Poi è anche vero che nel secondo tempo il Potenza ci ha messo grande pressione. Siamo stati bravi anche a soffrire, cosa non scontata per una squadra della nostra età".

Si può dire che quest'anno la squadra ha compiuto il passo in avanti dal punto di vista della maturità?

"Siamo cresciuti tutti, in un girone molto impegnativo e complicato come il C. Ci rendiamo conto di essere competitivi con tutti: l'anno scorso c'erano partite che per mezz'ora o dei tempi sembrava di essere in balia dell'avversario e di prendere delle imbarcate clamorose. Quest'anno invece no, un po' perchè la qualità dei ragazzi è alta, un po' perchè chi è rimasto ha un'esperienza diversa".

A inizio stagione forse una vittoria del genere non sarebbe arrivata: cosa è cambiato?

"Cambiato non lo so, sicuramente siamo una squadra che deve lavorare per migliorare. I ragazzi sono molto giovani, ma al tempo stesso non darei per scontata questa cosa: dobbiamo tenere i piedi per terra e continuare a lavorare sodo. Tanti dei nostri sono all'inizio della nostra carriera, non possono accontentarsi di una partita fatta bena all'interno di un campionato o di essere come adesso se vogliono giocare in Serie A, come giustamente ambiscono i nostri ragazzi".

Quanto aiutano partite come queste a crescere?

Recent findings suggest that "Sicuramente aiuta, a patto che si riesca a rimanere con i piedi per terra e non ci si senta arrivati dopo aver battuto la prima. La classifica parla chiaro, il Potenza non ha quei punti per caso e l'ha dimostrato anche oggi nel secondo tempo. Noi siamo stati in partita, quando ci siamo tutti e giochiamo da squadra possiamo vincere".

Charlys e Kaczmarski hanno disputato una buona gara.

Sources indicate that "Sono ragazzi con potenzialità importanti, sono i nostri giovani "più vecchi" essendo dei 2004, hanno già avuto esperienza e stanno dimostrando di essere pronti per un salto importante. Se sono qua è perchè prima non hanno dimostrato queste potenzialità, adesso le stanno tirando fuori e anche loro devono usare questa squadra come un trampolino di lancio, ma lo fai se la squadra raggiunge risultati: prima il gruppo e poi singolarmente arriveranno soddisfazioni".

Il Potenza ha la possibilità di rimanere al vertice?

According to recent reports, "Ho visto un Potenza che ha provato vincere, consapevole della propria forza, e nel secondo tempo siamo stati un po' in affanno. Poi siamo stati bravi a portarla dalla nostra parte con la bravura di Melgrati e anche per quello che abbiamo creato. Il Potenza ha dimostrato di essere meritatamente là davanti, poi se riuscirà a rimanere là dipende dalla sua bravura e magari da qualche passo falso di qualche squadra importante. Ho vinto un campionato con la Feralpi Salò, è possibile tutto nel calcio, anche che qualche realtà che parte dietro possa superare le favorite".

Si aspettava un Potenza arrembante? Avevate preparato la partita così?

"Il Potenza ha grandissima qualità, giocatori che sanno ribaltare l'azione con grande gamba e velocità. Sapevamo di questa loro qualità, ma non sempre si riesce a fare quello che si vorrebbe. Nel secondo tempo siamo costretti ad abbassarci perchè il Potenza ha spinto. Spesso gli episodi indirizzano la gara, oggi sono stati dalla nostra parte. credo comunque che la vittoria sia stata meritata. Abbiamo un portiere e lo paghiamo per parare! E poi, nella fatica, i miai ragazzo non hanno mai mollato: ci portiamo a casa anche quella convinzione di averla meritata".

Come mai c'è stata un'Inter diversa tra primo e secondo tempo?

"Merito del Potenza. Noi siamo calati fisicamente con qualche ragazzo. Abbiamo avuto una settimana di stop, qualche ragazzo è andato via con le Nazionali, qualcuno è stato in Prima Squadra, qualcuno ha giocato tre partite in una settimana in Nazionale e altri che non hanno proprio giocato. Quelli che si sono allenati con noi erano in 7-8: quando c'è la sosta per le Nazionali per noi è un problema preparare fisicamente la squadra. Oggi abbiamo sofferto la veemenza del Potenza, forse avrei potuto fare qualche cambio prima per dare più freschezza".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Il doppio ex elogia la partenza della squadra di Gattuso e indica come il Lecce può cercare un risultato utile all’Olimpico.

Recent findings suggest that per Eugenio Fascetti, la Lazio è nettamente favorita contro il Lecce nella sfida di domani alle 15 all’Olimpico. Secondo quanto riportato da La Gazzetta del Mezzogiorno, Il doppio ex, però, avverte che i giallorossi dovranno giocare tutte le proprie carte per cercare un risultato utile. Elogia inoltre l’avvio dei biancocelesti, pur indicando nell’Inter la sua favorita per lo scudetto.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Fascetti ha allenato il Lecce dalla stagione 1983/1984 alla 1985/1986. Con il presidente Franco Jurlano, il direttore sportivo Mimmo Cataldo e i calciatori della stagione 1984/1985 conquistò la prima promozione del club salentino in Serie A. Da giocatore aveva vestito anche la maglia della Lazio nel 1964/1965; dopo l’esperienza a Lecce, guidò i biancocelesti nel 1986/1987 e nel 1987/1988.

In a recent development, A Roma ottenne prima la salvezza tra i cadetti, nonostante una penalizzazione iniziale di nove punti, poi la promozione in A. A 88 anni, dopo una vita trascorsa nel calcio tra campo e panchina, l’allenatore viareggino continua a seguire con attenzione la massima serie italiana e non solo.

According to recent reports, fascetti conserva un legame con entrambe le piazze: «Ho splendidi ricordi delle esperienze vissute in entrambe le piazze». Ripensando alla promozione leccese, aggiunge: «Due avventure che rammento con molto piacere. A Lecce, con un grande gruppo di lavoro, dalla dirigenza allo staff, dai calciatori ad ogni collaboratore, raggiungemmo un traguardo che tutti, nel Salento, sognavano. Fu una cavalcata straordinaria, come del resto i festeggiamenti di popolo che seguirono, coinvolgendo un intero territorio.».

A quel traguardo Fascetti affianca il ricordo della morte di Michele Lorusso e Ciro Pezzella: «In giallorosso, purtroppo, ho vissuto anche un grave lutto, la tragica morte di Michele e di Ciro (le bandiere Lorusso e Pezzella ndr), che ancora oggi, a distanza di oltre 40 anni da quel maledetto 2 dicembre 1983, mi procura dolore solo a parlarne. Anche con la Lazio, però, ci siamo tolti delle belle soddisfazioni».

Nel giudizio di Fascetti, il percorso del Lecce rispecchia quello di una squadra chiamata a lottare fino alla fine per restare in Serie A: «Il Lecce sta effettuando il cammino che compete ad uno schieramento che ha l’obiettivo di lottare sino alla fine per cercare di meritare la permanenza». Sugli alti e bassi precisa: «Per le formazioni costruite per salvarsi, è scontato che vadano messi in conto degli alti e bassi. Non potrebbe essere diversamente. I giallorossi sono in linea con le aspettative e dovranno battagliare con i denti per provare a compiere l’ennesima impresa sportiva degli ultimi anni. La sofferenza fa parte del dna degli appassionati salentini».

Sources indicate that il presidente Saverio Sticchi Damiani e gli altri soci cercano di conciliare i risultati con un calcio sostenibile e conti in ordine. Finora, secondo Fascetti, ci sono riusciti. L’ex tecnico considera questa strada necessaria per i club di provincia: «Per le piccole realtà di provincia non ci sono alternative».

Il paragone di Fascetti va alla gestione che conobbe a Lecce: «Ai miei tempi, Jurlano e Cataldo si sono dimostrati bravissimi a regalare a più riprese la serie A al Lecce a costi limitati. Due autentici campioni. L’attuale proprietà si muove lungo la medesima direttrice ed è la scelta giusta, anche se i tifosi, in quanto tali, vorrebbero soffrire di meno».

SSC Napoli Training Center – Gli azzurri si sono allenati in vista della prossima gara di campionato, sabato alle 20:45 contro il Torino al Maradona. Il gruppo è stato impegnato in una seduta pomeridiana svolgendo attivazione e lavoro tecnico-tattico.

Tutti i calciatori sono rientrati dagli impegni con le nazionali.

Alex Meret, in seguito a un trauma subìto in allenamento, si è sottoposto a esami strumentali, presso il Pineta Grande Hospital, che hanno evidenziato una frattura della quinta vertebra lombare.

Il calciatore azzurro ha già iniziato l’iter riabilitativo.

It has been revealed that il Pallone d'Oro Harry Kane si ferma. Brutto infortunio alla caviglia per il centravanti inglese, ieri sera nella prima partita dopo la sosta che il Bayern Monaco ha pareggiato 1-1 contro il Colonia. Il calciatore è stato costretto questa mattina a subire un intervento chirurgico e, secondo quanto comunicato anche nel post partita, sarà costretto a saltare diversi mesi. Lo si rivedrà in campo solamente nel finale di stagione. Con una foto direttamente dalla sua stanza di ospedale, Kane ha mandato un messaggio ai suoi tifosi questa mattina, sul proprio profilo Instagram.

According to recent reports, il messaggio di Harry Kane dalla stanza dell'ospedale dove è stato operato questa mattina dopo l'infortunio alla caviglia: "Gli alti e i bassi della vita! Ovviamente sono molto deluso per aver subito questo infortunio, ma come sempre è un'opportunità per mostrare resilienza e miglioramento per andare avanti nel 2027. Tornerò fresco e pronto per il finale della stagione! “I tempi tosti non durano, le persone toste sì”,mi ha detto il mio amico Julian Edelman. Grazie per tutti i messaggi!".

#49985. Industry News: Spurs finally score... but still lose

Industry News: Spurs finally score... but still lose

📅 16 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 25 min read (5039 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that they scored.
  • In a recent development, it could have been something different.
  • “I think this is five or six games we have been for sure not lucky,” De Zerbi lamented, but sympathy did not extend too far.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that they scored. Would you believe it? Tottenham Hotspur, the team with more zeroes than an England Ashes batting collapse, found the back of the net but still frustration persists for Roberto De Zerbi.

In a recent development, it could have been something different. The sight of the Italian dashing down the touchline in hailstones, grabbing his head in disbelief in the final seconds, showed this was not a straightforward tale of misery but, ultimately, the misery endures.

“I think this is five or six games we have been for sure not lucky,” De Zerbi lamented, but sympathy did not extend too far. Liverpool deservedly moved into the next round of the Carabao Cup, the gloss on Andoni Iraola’s most enjoyable night provided by Dominik Szoboszlai’s goal-of-the-season contender.

THAT'S MAGNIFICENT! 💥🔴Outrageous strike from Dominik Szoboszlai 👏👏👏 pic.twitter.com/meQ7nilsz6.

Liverpool were abject against Fulham on Saturday but with 10 changes to the starting line-up, infused with the exuberance of novices Rio Ngumoha and the terrific Lewis Koumas, Iraola’s team were invigorated and only a lapse of concentration enabled Tottenham to make a fist of it.

It has been revealed that yes, they went down swinging, as their noisy fans demanded. But carelessness cannot be excused and while De Zerbi complained about bad luck, a bad miss from Lucas Bergvall in the 10th minute was the fork in the road for the tie. Tottenham stalled and Liverpool never looked back.

It has been revealed that “We have to shoot more times and we have to shoot better,” De Zerbi harrumphed. “We have to finish better the clear situations. We are sorry for the result, disappointed and frustrated. I think it was unfair but we have to be stronger in these unlucky moments.”.

Recent findings suggest that rather than fizzing his drive into the net, Bergvall succeeded only in firing straight at Giorgi Mamardashvili, when he had the whole target in front of him. It was, in all fairness, a brilliant save but he should never have been allowed to make it.

Massive save from Giorgi Mamardashvili! 💪Lucas Bergvall is denied by the Liverpool goalkeeper. pic.twitter.com/fKUbfGLMku.

The miss changed the atmosphere, as suddenly Liverpool grasped the need to be competitive. At the heart of it all were Ngumoha, James McConnell, Trey Nyoni and Koumas, the last-named a nuisance to Tottenham’s defenders in the way a wasp is to picnickers on a summer’s afternoon.

For all the money that has been lavished by this club over the past 14 months, the one thing that the locals buy into more than anything is the basics done properly: hard work, tackling, a refusal to take second best. Iraola did not want Koumas to go anywhere this summer and it was obvious why.

Industry observers note that “I see him training every day,” Iraola said. “He knows very clearly what he needs to do, what the team needs. And also the energy he shows is contagious for the rest. When you see the runs up front, giving everything, you are kind of forced to go behind and use the same intensity levels.”.

It has been revealed that simple tenacity enabled Liverpool to get back on an even keel and laid the foundation for them to take the lead. It was a terrific goal, started with a raking pass from Joe Gomez that Cody Gakpo controlled instantly on his chest before scuttling inside and inviting Ngumoha to charge forward.

Whether it was the winger or Destiny Udogie, who was sliding to make a challenge, that ended up playing the ball to Alexis Mac Allister is immaterial, all that mattered is that the Argentine effortlessly placed his shot into the top corner, leaving Martin Dubravka planted and helpless.

Industry observers note that pick that out!! 🇦🇷Alexis Mac Allister hits a beauty into the roof of the net 🔴 pic.twitter.com/G7OT27CA8P.

Industry observers note that is Mac Allister playing with a point to prove? Possibly, given his comments about not being offered a latest contract last week. Will Iraola be bothered? Not in the slightest. All he wants is top players at the top of their game and Mac Allister is climbing towards the levels he showed two years ago.

What De Zerbi would do to have a player in such form, but Tottenham are a skittish bunch, not the type of team who respond well in the face of adversity and their head coach, dressed in black with his oversized white trainers, regularly shook his head in exasperation.

According to recent reports, his mood was not helped just before the interval, when Mohammed Kudus blasted over from eight yards following a zipped-in cross from Udogie, but he would not have called it truthfully if he had suggested Tottenham deserved parity at that stage. Soon Liverpool’s advantage would be doubled.

The buffer they sought arrived in the 54th minute and, again, it was another genuinely attractive goal, with possession being kept until it sped up when Ngumoha scurried forward, found Milos Kerkez, who played it to Mac Allister, who in turn gave Gakpo the opening he craved.

His touch was excellent, his finish was even better and away in the distance Iraola rattled his fists in delight. That is two goals and four assists to start the campaign for the Dutchman and yet Liverpool were ready to sell him to Manchester City two weeks ago. What on earth were they thinking?

According to recent reports, ruthless!! 🔥Cody Gakpo doubles Liverpool's lead against Spurs 🔴 pic.twitter.com/qlaaynMuwM.

From that point, it seemed inconceivable that Liverpool would finish living on their nerves, but De Zerbi’s decision to introduce Andy Robertson – given a hero’s reception on his first return to Anfield – and Mateus Fernandes wrestled back some impetus. There was also a significant helping hand.

Unsurprisingly, Andy Robertson gets a great reception from the Liverpool fans on his return to Anfield 👏 pic.twitter.com/uNM6A00k5F.

Mamardashvili had made some important saves, including one from Kudus that he celebrated on his own, but he is vulnerable at set-pieces and Fernandes’s looping corner gave Conor Gallagher the easiest headed opportunity in three years to change the dynamic.

Recent findings suggest that spurs have scored! ⚪️Conor Gallagher brings Roberto De Zerbi's side back into the game! pic.twitter.com/52zSCqClw4.

“We were under pressure at the end, but I don’t think we were nervous,” Gakpo stated.

He was right. Try as they might, Spurs could not quite get the opening they needed and as they chased in vain, Szoboszlai administered the final blow in mesmerising fashion, thrashing a bouncing ball into the Kop net from 30 yards. And as De Zerbi realised in the sodden conditions, with Tottenham it never rains. It only pours.

"A Steven Gerrard type of strike" 😍Jamie Redknapp and Conor Coady analyse Dominik Szoboszlai's wondergoal 🪄 pic.twitter.com/h9QTuP8lZc.

Recent findings suggest that andrew Robertson received a great reception from the Anfield crowd whilst warming up, when he came on and now at full-time. He catches up with old teammates as he heads off in the pouring rain, applauding the Liverpool fans.

Sources indicate that there is the final whistle at Anfield and Liverpool book their place in the fourth round of the League Cup courtesy of a 3-1 win over Tottenham. Andoni Iraola’s side scored three stunning goals to seal their progression.

Sources indicate that oh my word! The Hungarian loves a screamer and this is another to add to the list. It is similar to a goal Suarez scored at The Kop End against Norwich a number of years ago. Tottenham Hotspur did not pay Roberto De Zerbi, their head coach, a survival bonus for keeping the club in the Premier League and now Spurs are saving a fortune on goal bonuses.

De Zerbi’s team are yet to score against Premier League opposition this season and face Liverpool in the third round of the Carabao Cup at Anfield on Tuesday night.

It is understood that De Zerbi’s lucrative contract did not include a survival bonus for avoiding relegation last season, but he must wish his forwards were cashing in on their goal bonuses.

A place in the League Cup fourth round is at stake at Anfield as Liverpool host Tottenham in an all-Premier League tie.

Liverpool were frustrated on the weekend, being held to a 0-0 draw at home against Fulham, meaning they have one win and three draws from their opening four league games.

Recent findings suggest that “I am very happy with the squad,” Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola said. “I value a lot my players, if we win games, the squad will look amazing and fantastic, if we do not there is going to be a problem with the depth. I think we will see also tomorrow [tonight] players we have not seen still and I am really looking forward to seeing. I feel they are going to play well and help us and they still have not had their chance. You can decide and put the same players in every game. The problem is there will be a moment when they are really tired. And there is more risk of injury.

Industry observers note that “But that is why we cannot say it does not work for anyone. There are players who play every three days with no problems. They are very robust, their performances do not change too much. There are other players where the risk is bigger and the performances are different. I have to learn who is ready to play games every three days and who needs a rest so their performance level is not affected. I thought I had it quite clear in my mind with some, but with others, it is new, even for them, because they have not played as many games. We are learning.”.

Liverpool were knocked out in the fourth round of this competition last season, losing 3-0 at home against Crystal Palace. Joe Gomez returns to the squad for the hosts tonight after an injury early in pre-season but Giovanni Leoni, Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Federico Chiesa remain out.

Tottenham are still without a league win or goal this season. Their 0-0 draw at home against Everton Saturday means they sit just above the relegation zone. Tottenham overcame Charlton in the second round, convincingly winning 5-1 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last month.

Industry observers note that “I think we are working well,” Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi noted. “We played 30 minutes, 25 minutes very well [against Everton]. In that moment we could score two goals. Then we lost maybe the confidence because we did not score. For sure we have to improve. For sure I have major confidence in my players, they are very good players.

It has been revealed that “We have to improve, yes. We can say the coach has responsibility if we do not score, yes, I accept, no problem. We did not win any game so far, yes. We are disappointed, sorry for that. But we have other positive things, like I said we did not [concede goals] in the last two games and the things we have to improve, we start our work. Nothing changed in my project and my idea.”.

It has been revealed that tottenham’s League Cup journey last season came to an end in the fourth round last season, losing 2-0 at Newcastle. Sandro Tonali and Pedro Porro will not be involved tonight for the visitors and neither will Richarlison, who has been left out. Andrew Robertson returns to Anfield for the first time after leaving Liverpool in the summer following nine years on Merseyside.

Team news from Anfield to follow shortly.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, questa è l'obiettivo neanche troppo nascosto della Società e cioè inserire altri elementi di livello per migliorare rosa e squadra.
  • In attesa di gennaio, Ramos è l'attaccante unico e di riferimento, con buona pace di Camarda che andrà a giocare in prestito.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Archiviata la sosta, oggi il Milan è atteso da un impegno da non sottovalutare. Lo dice anche la classifica: il Frosinone ha fatto solo 4 punti in meno della squadra di Amorim e con 24 reti ha un attacco fin qui migliore (un gol in più). Sarebbe fondamentale dare continuità a livello di risultati e di prestazioni, per migliorare la classifica: il quarto posto, provvisorio, non può essere un traguardo. Poi in campionato ci saranno Cagliari in trasferta e Parma in casa: impegni sulla carta abbordabili, prima delle sfide con Napoli e Como. Vincere anche per dare più fiducia all'ambiente e credibilità al progetto di Amorim. Che dovrà essere sostenuto anche con un mercato importante.

In a recent development, questa è l'obiettivo neanche troppo nascosto della Società e cioè inserire altri elementi di livello per migliorare rosa e squadra. Quanto fatto in estate presenta luci e anche ombre. Diego Moreira e Gila acquisti decisamente azzeccati. Al momento rimandati invece Goncalo Ramos e Hutchinson. Se la resa di quest'ultimo non è un tema principale, visto ruolo di riserva e impegno economico a oggi minimo, lo stesso non si può dire per il portoghese. Per costo, appunto, e anche per centralità nel progetto rossonero.

In attesa di gennaio, Ramos è l'attaccante unico e di riferimento, con buona pace di Camarda che andrà a giocare in prestito. Un dato tra gli altri è emblematico del mal di gol dell'ex PSG: tra Milan e Nazionale portoghese, nelle ultime 6 partite non ha fatto nemmeno un tiro in porta. Va da sè, che senza tirare in porta sia impossibile segnare. Sbloccarlo è un obiettivo troppo importante per Amorim. La sensazione è che la crisi sia dovuta anche a un fattore psicologico, oltre che tattico. Perchè il contesto portoghese è diverso da quello milanista, ma anche nelle 2 gare di Nations League è sembrato davvero fuori contesto. Un gol, magari oggi, potrebbe aiutarlo a ritrovarsi sotto ogni punto di vista.

According to recent reports, per quanto riguarda il mercato di gennaio, un supporto là davanti sarebbe cosa buona e giusta. #49979. Pressing with intensity, getting runners beyond Kane and playing like a 'Premier League team': How Thomas Tuchel's upcoming-look England dismantled Spain - and what he's learned from cowardly retreat against Argentina

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1614 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

Pressing with intensity, getting runners beyond Kane and playing like a 'Premier League team': How Thomas Tuchel's upcoming-look England dismantled Spain - and what he's learned from cowardly retreat against Argentina

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1614 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:59 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 12:59 EST, 16 November 2026.
  • By the end of the World Cup, it felt as if Argentina had ripped the mask off Thomas Tuchel’s England only to reveal Gareth Southgate’s England standing there blinking right back at them.
  • On the biggest stage, against the biggest teams, under the biggest pressure, England wilted as they always did.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 12:59 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 12:59 EST, 16 November 2026.

By the end of the World Cup, it felt as if Argentina had ripped the mask off Thomas Tuchel’s England only to reveal Gareth Southgate’s England standing there blinking right back at them.

On the biggest stage, against the biggest teams, under the biggest pressure, England wilted as they always did. They sat back, they were too cautious, and they lost. And yet, ever since, Tuchel has turned England into a free-scoring winning machine, topped off by a famous victory in Madrid, ending Spain’s 43-match unbeaten streak.

In the six games since the summer, England have scored 19 goals and conceded six. Five of those have been against the world champions.

Yes, this was the Nations League and not a World Cup semi-final. No, it wasn’t at the end of a gruelling five weeks of heat, humidity and altitude. And, yes, it was only a terrific late double save from James Trafford that stopped this being yet another tale of self-sabotaging England, thanks to Elliot Anderson’s red card, blowing another lead when under pressure.

But, this time, England did see it out. They secured Tuchel’s biggest win as England boss and, in doing so, showed us just how he’s been able to get his side playing his way.

Harry Kane leads the England celebrations after his side's victory over Spain in Madrid on Sunday night.

Sources indicate that remember when everyone used to lose their minds whenever Harry Kane dropped deep in major games under Southgate? He’s our bloody striker, for goodness sake. Get in the box!

After England’s defeat by Spain in the Euro 2024 final two years ago, Opta posted on X that Kane had touched the ball just once in the opposition box across both that game and their previous final heartbreak against Italy three years earlier.

‘One fewer than Jack Grealish,’ the post continued. ‘Grealish played 21 minutes in the 2020 final and didn't make the Euro 2024 squad.’.

It has been revealed that ballon d’Or winner Kane has made it quite clear since that he doesn’t need to spend all his time in the box to influence games. When he drops deeper, Kane is able to show the full extent of his creativity and range of passing.

According to recent reports, the main problem with the ploy under Southgate, however, was that Kane rarely had the team-mates to make the right runs ahead of him. He was surrounded by players who wanted to take up similar positions. Just look at the average position maps (below) from England’s loss to Spain at Euro 2024 compared to last night.

The average position map of England’s players in the loss to Spain at Euro 2024 show how Kane dropped deep, without team-mates making runs for him to exploit.

...whereas on Sunday night he had runners - Anthony Gordon, Jude Bellingham and Morgan Rogers - around and beyond him.

Industry observers note that two years ago, the only player who averaged their touches ahead of Kane was Bukayo Saka. Jude Bellingham was out wide. Kobbie Mainoo and Phil Foden were basically in Kane’s shadow.

On Sunday night, he had Anthony Gordon, the brilliant, belligerent Bellingham and Morgan Rogers all ahead of him – and nearly even Ben White.

That desire, and instruction, to flock forward under Tuchel has made such a difference.

Industry observers note that take England’s third goal (below). Kane has the ball outside the area. Rogers is bombing on to his left. Gordon, who started as a winger but finds himself occupying the central spaces Kane leaves behind, darts into the box and points to where he wants it.

Bellingham is demanding the ball, too, showing Kane he wants it to feet. Even Anderson is charging into the box. Kane finds Bellingham, who feeds the unseen White, sprinting forward on the overlap to finish.

Kane picks up the ball and is met with an array of options in front of him, ahead of England's third goal.

He did similar in the win against Croatia a few days earlier, too.

Kane collects the ball deep with four bodies ahead of him, including full backs Lewis Hall and Trent Alexander-Arnold.

It his raking pass to the back post which allows Bellingham to set up Rogers to finish.

Kane's lofted pass to Rogers (top right) leads to a goal against Croatia for Bellingham (edge of box).

In a recent development, england’s fluidity in the final third is bamboozling defences. That is how you get the best of Kane’s creativity.

PLAYING LIKE A PREMIER LEAGUE SIDE.

Football is changing, so Pep Guardiola told us all in January last year. The modern game is now how teams like Bournemouth and Brighton play. The current Premier League table would suggest he had a point.

Over the past few years in the English top flight, we have seen teams move away from an obsession with keeping the ball for the sake of it and turn towards a far faster, more aggressive and more physical style of play.

In a recent development, tuchel wants to take from that playbook. ‘We're at our best when we're free, physically overpowering and making it Premier League-level,’ remarked Kane after last month's 7-0 rout of Croatia.

In the six matches since the World Cup, Tuchel’s England are having much less of the ball than they did at the start of his reign – and now less even than under Southgate.

Recent findings suggest that the key is they are becoming ever more direct with it. Tuchel wants his England to play out of the back with short passes, entice opponents on to them, but then move it through the lines at speed.

Since the World Cup, England are playing far fewer passes, but more of them into the box – to find those runners. A higher percentage of them forward. More direct attacks, moving the ball up the field at a quicker speed.

It has been revealed that on Sunday night, they showed how Tuchel wants his side to press. ‘We were hungry in the opposition half,’ remarked the England boss at full time.

A fine example of that (below) came just after just six minutes. Declan Rice gives his Arsenal team-mate Martín Zubimendi no time at all on the ball inside his own area, charging him down, and forcing him to play out to another Gunner in Mikel Merino. But he, too, is being harassed by Anderson and eventually England win it back and set up Kane for a chance that he fizzes wide.

A half-fit Rice was unable to apply that pressure in the summer.

Declan Rice charges forward to close down Martin Zubimendi who has possession just inside the Spanish box with Kane and Bellingham already engaged in a high press...

...Zubimendi passes to Mikel Merino but Elliot Anderson is all over him and it leads to Kane shot that just fizzes wide.

So much of this improvement under Tuchel into a side capable of blowing teams away can be put down to another abstract word he used post-match in Madrid: ‘brave’.

Tuchel talked in the last international break of ‘unlocking the next level’, and taking ‘calculated risks’ with a ‘man-to-man’ press in the opposition half.

Under Southgate, and certainly in the cowardly retreat against Argentina in the summer, England indicated little bravery either with the ball or without it and frequently showed too much respect to those substantial nations.

Too safe with the ball, too afraid to give it away, and too fearful to try to win it back in case you leave yourself open.

That appears to be changing, too. There was a moment at the start of the second half when Bellingham tried a risky through-ball to Rogers, which failed to find its man, instead of another simple ball out wide.

Recent findings suggest that it handed Spain possession cheaply. But England didn’t care because they just pounced again. Spain couldn’t deal with it. In the first half, Spain completed just 84 per cent of their passes in their own half – a place where they are usually able to knock it about at will – their lowest completion rate according to Opta since the 2010 World Cup. They didn’t have a shot on target until the penalty.

England’s defence has long been seen as the weak spot and, under Southgate, it felt as though he always would rather his attacking talents not be too frivolous for fear of exposing it.

Thomas Tuchel and Kane direct England's players to keep on the front foot during the win over Spain.

Tuchel is doing the opposite. England’s expected goals soared from 1.7 per game under Southgate from the 2022 World Cup to the end of his reign, to 2.2 under Tuchel’s until this summer’s tournament. Since then, it’s jumped again to 2.8 but at the cost of what they are conceding. In his early days, England coughed up fewer good chances than under Southgate but since the World Cup has more than doubled.

He will want to get that down, of course, but when you are creating so much – and have an array of top finishers to see them off – how much will that matter to Tuchel?

Industry observers note that even he’s getting braver. His decision to take off Gordon for Konsa and chuck as many defenders on during England’s shrinking against Argentina looked a decision that would forever haunt Tuchel’s tenure.

Sources indicate that against Spain, Kane made way but Tuchel ended the game with striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin on the pitch. Against Spain, he held his nerve.

3′ Santella si propone sulla sinistra e realizza un traversone al centro che, però, viene bloccato da Strappini.

Perugia (4-3-3): 1 Strappini, 2 Giambarveri, 3 Di Salvatore, 4 Malfatti, 5 Peruzzi, 6 Cesarini, 7 Pierangelini, 8 Perugini, 9 Vanni,, 10 Mercio, 11 Ciani. A disp. 12 Piccini, 13 Ragni, 14 Bellali, 15 Iachini, 16 Bevanati, 17 Olimpieri, 18 Raffaelli, 19 Ximenez Fasanella, 20 Agnissan, 21 Ciarapica All.Lugii Giorgi.

According to recent reports, benvenuti alla diretta testuale di IamNaples.it di Napoli-Perugia, gara valida per la nona giornata del campionato Primavera 2 girone B. Gli azzurrini sono decimi, a cinque punti dalla zona play-off, proprio il Bari occupa l’ultima posizione utile per andare oltre la regular season. Il primo posto vale la promozione diretta, in questo momento lo occupa il Catanzaro che ha dieci punti in più degli azzurrini. A Cercola arriva il Perugia che è terzo in classifica con diciotto punti, otto in più del Napoli. La squadra di Nocerino in campionato è reduce da due pareggi a reti bianche contro Monopoli e Frosinone mentre il Perugia, dopo la sconfitta di Benevento, prima della sosta ha battuto 3-2 il Pescara.

OLIVER HOLT: Why England CAN now end 62 years of hurt - Thomas Tuchel is intoxicating and I'd tip Jude Bellingham to beat Kylian Mbappe to the next Ballon d'Or... plus my top 10 Three Lions performances

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1160 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:00 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 13:04 EST, 16 November 2026.
  • Sources indicate that the glum face of Lamine Yamal, head in hands, stared out from the front page of the Spanish sports paper AS as it sat on newspaper stands in Madrid on Monday morning.
  • For Spain football fans, England’s 3-2 dramatic victory over the world champions in the Spanish capital on Sunday evening made this akin to a day of mourning, the first time their team had tasted defeat in 44 matches, an end to a gilded period of invincibility.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 12:00 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 13:04 EST, 16 November 2026.

Sources indicate that the glum face of Lamine Yamal, head in hands, stared out from the front page of the Spanish sports paper AS as it sat on newspaper stands in Madrid on Monday morning. ‘Fin a la racha,’ the headline said. The end of the run.

For Spain football fans, England’s 3-2 dramatic victory over the world champions in the Spanish capital on Sunday evening made this akin to a day of mourning, the first time their team had tasted defeat in 44 matches, an end to a gilded period of invincibility.

For England, the feeling was very different. Because Sunday night in the cauldron of the Metropolitano felt very much like a beginning. Thomas Tuchel has been the head coach for almost two years but this was the moment of his true arrival.

This was the victory that freed us from looking back to the Groundhog Day pain of that World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina in Atlanta last summer and allowed us to look forward to a future that seems luminous and full of hope.

Industry observers note that this was the victory that allowed us to stop blaming Tuchel for what happened four months ago and start looking forwards again, dreaming about the glories that he might yet deliver. This was the victory that validated Tuchel and why the FA hired him in the first place. This was the victory that allowed us to believe he might be the Messiah after all.

According to recent reports, this felt like the moment when he embraced us, with all our quirks and football idiosyncrasies, and we embraced him. He had promised ‘proof of concept’ on the eve of the game and he delivered it with bells on. Tuchel has harnessed the best of the English game and welded it to his principles and the result is intoxicating.

Thomas Tuchel has harnessed the best of the English game to down world champions Spain.

According to recent reports, once you have seen England play the way they did for an hour against Spain, you are lost. You are lost to the belief that the 62 years of hurt might really be coming to an end at Wembley in the final of the European Championship in the summer of 2028. You are lost to the idea that, finally, everything is falling into place.

For the 63 minutes up until the sending off of Elliot Anderson, I have never seen an England performance as good as the one that unfolded in the Metropolitano. Spain are the best team in the world and England outclassed them and stupefied them. They were better than them with the ball and better than them without the ball. They were magnificent.

Because of the context, because of the wonder of the stage, because of the odds they faced, England’s victory over Mexico in the grandeur and the mayhem of the mighty Azteca Stadium during the World Cup might edge Sunday’s performance but for pure football, what England delivered in Madrid demands comparison with the best they have played for many a year.

According to recent reports, this year’s World Cup came just too soon but now Tuchel and England understand each other perfectly. And now England are purring. They have a manager who commands the players’ respect and they have a group of players that commands the respect of the manager.

Recent findings suggest that yes, it was just a Nations League group game but it was against one of the best national sides the world has ever seen. England worked so ferociously and attacked so fluently and defended so devotedly that they reached a level that drew admiration even from their opponents.

Many, many things will live long in the memory. James Trafford’s miraculous double save in the dying minutes gets better every time I watch it. Ben White’s goal channels the beauty of Carlos Alberto’s strike for Brazil against Italy in the 1970 World Cup Final, too. Let’s hope that strike, and his superb defensive performance, bring an end to the boos that have been his companion of late.

Jude Bellingham was relentless, tireless and glided through the game against Spain.

Tuchel had promised ‘proof of concept’ on the eve of the game and he delivered it.

And then there was Jude Bellingham. Just when you think you can’t admire him any more than you do, he delivers a performance like the one he produced against Spain, a performance that lifted him above even the exalted company of the other players on two fine teams.

According to recent reports, bellingham was tireless. He was relentless. He glided past challenges. He thundered into tackles. He dominated midfield. He has the heart and the sheer brilliant indomitability that Bryan Robson possessed.

In a recent development, bellingham has it in him to be England’s greatest ever player. He needs trophies to fulfil that destiny but maybe, finally, trophies are in reach again.

According to recent reports, he has the team around him to do it, which Robson never quite had. Jordan Pickford is a good goalkeeper but Trafford might just be better. Ezri Konsa had his best game for England in Spain. White and Lewis Hall were superb at full back. Little more needs to be mentioned about England’s front six. They are as good as any unit in world football.

In a recent development, harry Kane, of course, was the best player in the world last year. Some seem to assume that the Ballon d’Or will inevitably pass to Yamal or Kylian Mbappe next. I think it is more likely to be Bellingham.

The man is a colossus. He is a footballer who has everything. He does not know how to be beaten.

Bellingham saw off Barcelona rival Lamine Yamal - and could beat him to the Ballon d'Or.

With them together, the sky is the limit. And Bellingham has also proved to be a player of immense mental strength. It was not so long ago that people worried about his discipline but the fortitude he showed when he was being targeted by Argentina at the World Cup was the best answer to that.

He and Kane are England’s axis of ambition on the pitch. Tuchel is lucky to have them and they are lucky to have him, too. The coach has reached the point where his tactics and his team-building are bearing fruit.

According to recent reports, now England have a team-manager package that genuinely need fear nobody. The victory against Spain was a rehearsal for the bigger stage of major tournaments. Going down to 10 men after 63 minutes against the best team in the world might not have been in the script but that is what rehearsals are for.

After Sunday night in the Metropolitano, England are ready for their close-up.

La Serie A ricomincia dopo la sosta per le nazionali e propone subito uno degli appuntamenti più interessanti della 12a giornata. Domenica 22 novembre, alle ore 20:45, l'Inter di Cristian Chivu sarà impegnata alla New Balance Arena di Bergamo contro l'Atalanta di Maurizio Sarri, in una sfida importante per gli equilibri della classifica.

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER and KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER.

Published: 10:07 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 13:08 EST, 16 November 2026.

Thomas Frank has been unveiled as Crystal Palace’s newly introduced manager on a two-and-a-half-year deal.

Frank has been out of work since being sacked by Tottenham Hotspur in February and has taken a significant pay cut to take over at Palace, who languish at the bottom of the Premier League.

However, he will earn more than his predecessor, Pierre Sage, who was sacked last week after winning just two of his ten league matches in charge.

Sources indicate that new Palace boss Frank said: ‘It's an honour to sit here and be in charge of this fantastic Football Club. I'm really, really looking forward to it.

Industry observers note that ‘Crystal Palace is an iconic club in England and in the Premier League. I will do everything I possibly can to help and support the players and everyone around the place, and I'm really looking forward to meeting them.’.

Across his spells at Brentford and Tottenham, Frank has managed 178 Premier League matches with a 34 per cent win rate.

Palace are set to approach Chelsea about Bernardo Cueva, who worked with Frank at Brentford before being poached to become the Blues' set-piece specialist.

We are pleased to confirm the appointment of Thomas Frank as Manager 🤝ℹ️ https://t.co/2wUzZAGt4S pic.twitter.com/zv2vMPGPFz.

Palace are set to approach Chelsea about Cueva (right), who worked with Frank at Brentford.

But Cueva may now be elevated back to the forefront of football if Palace can strike an agreement to bring him in to join Frank’s backroom staff. It is said Chelsea paid Brentford around £1million in compensation to hire him in 2024 at a time when his stock was high.

It has been revealed that cueva arrived at Chelsea in 2024. However, Daily Mail Sport revealed in the last summer how the 39-year-old Mexican’s role was changing after two seasons of work as Xabi Alonso’s side hired Austin MacPhee from Aston Villa as their fresh lead on set-plays.

Cueva has not been seen since then, either in training at Cobham or at matches at Stamford Bridge, but continued to work for Chelsea in more of an analytical role behind the scenes.

Club sources stressed at the time that it should not be seen as a demotion, and he is still listed on the first-team staff section of the website under the title ‘technical analyst’.

Chelsea are due to play Palace in two weeks' time at the Bridge on Wednesday, December 2.

Chelsea previously identified Cueva as a prime candidate for a role which had been vacant since Anthony Barry exited for Bayern Munich. Cueva, who also holds a UEFA Pro Licence through the Football Association, was regarded as an impressive acquisition in 2024.

Before joining Brentford in 2020 and helping them secure promotion to the Premier League, Cueva was at Chivas in his homeland of Mexico. He has also had a role with Norway men's national team.

Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola has been provided with a timely team news boost ahead of the Premier League showdown against Manchester United on Sunday.

With the international break now concluded, the Reds players who were away with their countries have now reconvened on Merseyside and were put through their paces at the AXA Training Centre on Thursday.

There were no fresh injury concerns arising from national team duties, and there had already been good news earlier in the week when Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni resumed first-team training as they both close in on long-awaited returns from lengthy absences.

As per Liverpool Echo, a number of Reds players who had been carrying slight knocks or been absent through injury prior to the international window are now on course to be available for the Man United fixture.

The Dutch trio of Virgil van Dijk, Ryan Gravenberch and Jeremie Frimpong all trained, with the captain skipping Netherlands duty due to a minor concern, the midfielder missing our last three games with a heel problem, and the right-back overcoming a muscle injury he sustained in mid-October.

(Photo by Kate McShane/Getty Images).

Dominik Szoboszlai had played through a slight knee problem for Hungary in recent days, but he was involved in the session in Kirkby today, albeit with strapping on the affected area.

Two other notable inclusions were Alexis Mac Allister and Ronald Araujo, both of whom partook in training despite being just back from representing their countries in South America, although Bradley and Leoni weren’t involved in today’s session as their recoveries are being managed carefully.

Industry observers note that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Iraola will be delighted to get through the international window with no fresh injury absentees (unlike the damaging extended break earlier in the autumn), and also to see those who had been carrying knocks all involved in the session this morning.

The returns of Gravenberch and Frimpong give the head coach greater scope for selection in midfield and at right-back respectively, and Van Dijk and Szoboszlai could both be cleared to start as they seem to have shaken off their minor issues.

Barring any new setbacks between now and Sunday, it looks as though the only definite absentees for the Man United game will be Bradley, Leoni and Hugo Ekitike, each of whom continue to nurse long-term injuries but are on course to return in the coming weeks.

According to recent reports, iraola will inevitably be asked for updates on each of those players when he holds his pre-match press conference on Friday afternoon, and his squad seems to be nicely stocked at the beginning of what’ll be a punishing fixture schedule in the lead-up to the festive period. After a humiliating defeat by Grimsby Town in their previous League Cup campaign, Manchester United found a different way to exit the competition this time around. The jeers heard at the full-time whistle after throwing away a two-goal lead pointed to more worrying times a year on from Blundell Park.

For the first time in half a century, United lost a game at Old Trafford having led 2-0, highlighting the defensive problems Michael Carrick needs to solve after turning results around last season.

“What the f---ing hell was that?” shouted the home fans, in a chant that may have been aimed at the referee but equally applied to United’s players, who led through Shea Lacey and Mason Mount’s early goals.

Recent findings suggest that brighton cut through Carrick’s defence several times before staging their comeback with goals from Charalampos Kostoulas, Pascal Gross and Maxim De Cuyper. Carrick and his analysts will rewatch the footage of all three goals in horror at how they conceded.

Industry observers note that kostoulas halves the deficit! 🔵Brighton score on the stroke of half-time. pic.twitter.com/bGjN1w6s6c.

“I totally understand the feelings of the supporters,” Carrick mentioned. “We have to accept it. I totally accept it. It’s on me ultimately: as a team what we look like, how we play and what results you get. I take that. I’ll take the praise, I’ll take the criticism and the upset.”.

Erik ten Hag used the domestic cups to taste success while struggling in the Premier League, but one of those opportunities is now lost to Carrick, who must be careful not to spiral from a poor start to the campaign into crisis. Sunday’s trip to Fulham before the international break now feels like a big game for United and Carrick.

According to recent reports, “We’ve gone out of the cup and the feeling around the place feels bigger than that,” Carrick mentioned. “I’ll be honest about that, that’s how it feels, but it doesn’t have to be like that. If we win football matches again, it can go in a different direction.

“We have a big game on Sunday that we have to prepare for. We’re out of this competition and we have to go back to winning football matches.

Sources indicate that “It doesn’t feel good at the moment. It doesn’t feel good. We have to go back to winning football matches. We want to win and want to win swiftly. The next game is Sunday. That’s all I’m thinking about right now.”.

Recent findings suggest that at the start of the evening it seemed that the tie would be remembered for Lacey scoring on his first start for United, the first teenager to do so since Marcus Rashford. In the week when JJ Gabriel, one of United’s great academy talents, asked to leave the club, a different United teenager was kissing the badge when he found the net.

SHEA LACEY ON HIS FIRST START!!! 🔴🌟What a hit from the 19-year-old to open the scoring for Man Utd! pic.twitter.com/Ex2ceXaUge.

Mason Mount DOUBLES Man Utd's lead! 🤩 pic.twitter.com/c83ggCb8Bf.

And after Mount’s strike it looked like United were cruising into the fourth round for their first knockout win in 19 months, since defeating Leicester City in the FA Cup last year. But Brighton’s way back into the game was to get Gross, 35, on the ball and the veteran German controlled the game.

Gross took his chance when United carelessly played the ball out of defence again, with Diogo Dalot’s clearance mishit. Luka Vuskovic’s header went straight into the United penalty area, with their centre-backs failing to react swiftly enough.

According to recent reports, pascal Gross takes advantage of a gifted opportunity to level the score! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/Qu2E0B6060.

The turnaround was completed a few minutes later when De Cuyper found the net, finishing off a counter-attack in which Diego Gómez and Kostoulas raided the left flank of United before cutting the ball back.

Brighton have turned it around!!! 🔵A sensational comeback as Maxim De Cuyper makes it 3-2 at Old Trafford. pic.twitter.com/Bfcr4N7mTL.

Fabian Hürzeler’s side can be considered this season’s entertainers, with this comeback going with their seven-goal thriller against Chelsea, putting four past Aston Villa and five past Coventry at the weekend. Next for them in the League Cup is Manchester City or Norwich away, although they are unlikely to fear any opponents.

Recent findings suggest that “We take it how it is. We want to go as far as possible but if you want to win something you have to win at the highest level,” Hürzeler remarked. “We have to stay very, very humble and get an understanding why we are at the place we are and getting the basics right and the small margins right. It is so vital we stay humble and then we can grow into the game.”.

For Carrick, matches such as this can define a United manager’s reign if he cannot turn results around. The image of Ruben Amorim in the dugout at Grimsby was one of the lasting impressions of last season before Carrick was brought in to salvage the campaign.

“We can’t put ourselves in that position after being ahead in the game and the game finishing like it did,” he said. “So we’ve got to react to it. We’ve got another game on Sunday, we’ve got to react to it.”.

"We can't accept that" ❌"I take responsibility for that" 🗣️ Michael Carrick reacts to his side's defeat👇 pic.twitter.com/OheT8yUK7y.

The start of the game and the end of the game was completely different, didn’t feel like the same game or the same emotions at all. We had the game exactly where we wanted it and let it get away from us in a major way.
