💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that manchester City have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought by the Premier League over breaches of its financial rules.
  • City face a range of sanctions from a fine to points deductions and even expulsion from the Premier League.
  • If the verdict is upheld, with City expected to appeal, it will also raise question marks over the 20 trophies the club have won under Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, whose Abu Dhabi group took over in 2008.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that manchester City have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought by the Premier League over breaches of its financial rules. It is a decision that, if upheld, would equate to one of the biggest scandals in football history.

City face a range of sanctions from a fine to points deductions and even expulsion from the Premier League. Or a combination of all, under rule W51 of its handbook. No punishment has yet been confirmed.

If the verdict is upheld, with City expected to appeal, it will also raise question marks over the 20 trophies the club have won under Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, whose Abu Dhabi group took over in 2008.

The charges can be broken down into five categories and relate to a period from 2009-23 in which City won six League Cups, three FA Cups, seven league titles and the Champions League. There is the provision for removing past titles, but that would appear remote.

City have been the dominant force in English football for most of that time, but that status is under threat with a verdict that will send shockwaves around Europe and could have huge ramifications for the club.

That is unless they can win an appeal, with sources cautioning it still may take up to another two to three years for the case to be resolved, following on from an already five-year investigation.

The Premier League’s rules provide for an independent appeal board with broad powers, including the ability to uphold, vary or overturn the independent commission’s decision.

It would therefore appear that despite the verdict, the case is far from being resolved and punishment decided. The details of the commission’s findings, when published, will be crucial to determining what happens next.

But if it is upheld, the verdict also opens up the possibility of City facing legal action from other clubs who feel they missed out on trophies and even merit money from league placings.

It is understood Premier League clubs are already discussing legal action and possible compensation claims as a result of the guilty verdict.

Industry observers note that each of those cases would have to be held individually, potentially leading to years more of litigation. Conversely, if City win their appeal, they too could take legal action against the Premier League the damage caused to their reputation.

There has not yet been an official confirmation of the independent panel’s verdict from the Premier League. The Premier League declined to comment.

Recent findings suggest that however, several sources have told Telegraph Sport that the panel has found City guilty of all but one of the charges they faced. The one that has not been proved is said to be one of the most serious of the 115.

The damning verdict for City is a major new test of fragile UK relations with the United Arab Emirates, with whom bilateral trade was worth £25bn last year. Redacted freedom of information documents, seen by Telegraph Sport, show Abu Dhabi hosted UK government officials including Lord Stockwood, then investment minister, as recently as February. Khaldoon Al Mubarak, the City chairman and trusted adviser to the UAE president, was present at the meeting. Government notes from the meeting recorded that he “noted they are very proud of what they have achieved through their investments in Manchester”.

The Government previously caused acrimony among senior leaders in Abu Dhabi after putting forward legislation to ban foreign states from owning UK newspapers and news magazines. The intervention prompted the collapse of a takeover of The Telegraph in April 2024, which was largely funded by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the owner of City and vice-president and deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates.

The previous UK government has admitted its embassy in Abu Dhabi and the Foreign Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) in London discussed the charges levelled at City by the Premier League. However it refused to disclose the correspondence.

Sources indicate that city have steadfastly maintained they are innocent, promising “irrefutable” evidence in support of their position, and had assembled some of the most expensive lawyers in the country to argue their case. Despite the verdict, the club are understood to be confident that it will win the argument in the end. Senior figures are said to be calm about the latest development, as significant as it seems.

It has been revealed that city rebuilt their team this summer and it is understood that signings were brought in on conventional player contracts, rather than terms including clauses triggered in the event of a heavy punishment. Given the club have consistently denied breaching financial regulations, and their deals for new players to work with head coach Enzo Maresca underlines their position.

On Friday, a City spokesman stated: “The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such, Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the club’s statement of February 2023.

“The club have diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.”.

Sources close to Pep Guardiola, the former City manager who stepped down last summer after 10 years of remarkable success at the club, including a treble triumph in 2023 and an unprecedented fourth straight league title in 2024, insist he has not been informed of any verdict.

In the days after City were first charged, Guardiola mounted a fierce defence of the club, claiming: “I am fully convinced we will be [proved] innocent.”.

The verdict vindicates the Premier League’s decision to launch an investigation after explosive allegations that City had routinely broken financial rules were first made in Der Spiegel in 2018 based on the Football Leaks documents.

Uefa previously accused City of breaches of its financial regulations and revealed in 2020 that it was suspending the club from the Champions League for two years for “overstating” sponsorship revenue between 2012 and 2016.

Sources indicate that city denied the Uefa charges and, after an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport, the two-year ban was overturned. Cas found that a number of the claims brought by Uefa had fallen outside a five-year “time bar” and others were “not established”.

Sources indicate that it did, however, still impose a €10m fine after ruling that City failed to cooperate with investigators. City had previously also agreed a settlement with Uefa of €20m in 2014 following an investigation into their finances.

Legal experts agreed that the commission’s verdict is far from the end of the case. Yasin Patel, barrister at Church Court Chambers, remarked: “City’s lawyers will now analyse this decision and look at the options open to them to appeal, which may include procedural impropriety, wrongful interpretation of law, and legal errors – importantly, they can guarantee an appeal.

Industry observers note that “Sanctions could include a major fine, points deduction, relegation or even all three. Factoring in whether titles and trophies should be stripped, whether other clubs have been robbed of further revenue and opportunities due to City’s wrongdoings and losses incurred, we safely say that this is only the first chapter of a long-running legal saga that will not end any time soon.”.

Ian Hargreaves, partner with specialist disputes firm Quillon Law, remarked the verdict was “not the end of the story but the beginning of a new phase”, and added: “There is also the question of whether the panel’s decision can withstand a hard-fought appeal, and on what grounds any challenge might be brought. Much will depend on the detail of the panel’s findings and reasoning, which will inevitably be closely scrutinised by both sides.”.

Former Manchester City midfielder Rodri, who won the Ballon d’Or during his trophy-laden spell at the club, said he believed the club were innocent.

“For the players, it’s different than it is for journalists. I can understand all opinions, but we try to stay positive,” the Spain midfielder mentioned while on international duty.

Industry observers note that “When you see all the people who worked hard at City to achieve success, you know what we achieved can’t be taken away. It wasn’t paid for with money, but with effort and teamwork. Everything we achieved was deserved; we marked one of the great eras of English football. I believe in the club’s innocence – we already went through this in 2020.”.

Andy Burnham, the Prime Minister, noted: “I think we would all need to study the independent commission’s report in some considerable detail before reaching any conclusions.”.

Zohran Kwame Mamdani, the mayor of New York, posted “114” in relation to the charges while former Manchester United players David de Gea and Rio Ferdinand both asked whether they should be due winner’s medals from past seasons.

The Premier League statement in February 2023 said that “a number of alleged breaches” had been referred to an independent commission. It then detailed each specific rule against each season in which the alleged breach took place. The precise number was not clear from the statement and led to varying reports between 115 and 130. Friday’s news suggested the figure was 115.

Industry observers note that all the way to 2009-10, the first full season following the club’s takeover by Sheikh Mansour, who is a member of the Abu Dhabi Royal family and the vice president of the United Arab Emirates. There were charges relating to all 14 seasons until the Premier League completed their investigation during the 2022-23 campaign. In that time, City won seven Premier League titles, six League Cups, three FA Cups and the Champions League. They have since won another league title – the first club to do so four times in a row – as well as the Uefa Super Cup, the Fifa Club World Cup and the FA Cup and League Cup double last season.

They can be split into five groups. The biggest relates to the seasons from 2009-10 until 2017-18 and the requirement for clubs to provide accurate financial information and act in the utmost good faith.

In a recent development, the next set of rules concern the full disclosure of manager and player payments. The alleged manager breaches related to the period between 2009-10 and 2012-13, when Roberto Mancini was leading the team. The alleged breaches with respect to player payments relate to all of the seasons between 2010-11 and 2015-16.

As well as providing financial detail, clubs were required to meet Uefa and Premier League rules which were designed to bring a club’s spending broadly in line with their income by placing set limits on losses. City were charged with breaches of Uefa’s licencing and financial fair play rules from 2013-14 until 2017-18, and the Premier League’s profit and sustainability rules from 2015-16 until 2017-18.

The final set of charges spanned the five seasons during which City were being investigated by the Premier League and rules that require members to cooperate in the utmost good faith by providing information and documents.

According to recent reports, A full picture will only emerge when the commission publishes its findings but we know that the Premier League investigation began in December 2018 following allegations in the German newspaper Der Spiegel based on the Football Leaks documents. These included alleged payments to former manager Mancini for consultancy work at an Abu Dhabi-based club that was separate to his regular contract at City.

We also know that City were alleged to have breached rules over setting out image rights payments to players in their club contract. Der Spiegel reported that the Premier League investigation also focused on payments to under-age players, as well as whether club sponsors were paying for commercial deals themselves or a significant proportion was in fact effectively coming from owner Sheikh Mansour.

In a recent development, city have always denied breaking any rules. In response to the Premier League statement about the alleged breaches, they stated that they have “irrefutable evidence” to support their position and “look forward to this matter being put to rest once and for all.”.

At the start of the hearing in September 2024, Guardiola also noted: “Wait for the independent panel. We believe we have not done anything wrong.”.

In a recent development, of the Football Leaks documents, City stated: “We will not be providing any comment on out-of-context materials. The attempt to damage the club’s reputation is organised and clear.”.

And among the team's most glaring underperformers – according to some observers in France – were Chelsea's Malo Gusto, Bournemouth's Adrien Truffert and Liverpool's £123million summer signing Bradley Barcola.

French outlet RMC Sport was particularly critical of the pair, with journalist Alexandre Jaquin describing Gusto as 'probably the one who disappointed the most during this second international window of the Zidane era'.

Jaquin added: 'Fielded in Italy despite little playing time with Chelsea, the right-back completely fell into the San Siro furnace.

Malo Gusto struggled has been under fire from the French media after a string of poor performances under Zinedine Zidane.

The honeymoon period is over for Zidane, according to French media.

RMC was not much kinder to Barcola as well, concluding: 'The Liverpool winger was one of the few to start both matches in November. But in the end, it didn't really take off, neither in Italy nor against Turkey.

'Sometimes on his left flank, sometimes in a false nine, the former PSG supersub was often imprecise in his final moves. Like his failed one-on-one against the Turks, the Lyon native lacked accuracy and composure to make the opposing goal tremble.'.

Even newcomer Adrien Truffert was not afforded some sympathy as Jaquin noted: 'After a rather satisfying debut in October, the Bournemouth left-back benefited from the trust of Zinedine Zidane, who played him in Italy. But despite his efforts, the Cherries player delivered a very mixed performance.'.

This recent criticism adds to growing dissatisfaction in France with the overall state of the national team under Zidane.

Liverpool's £123million man is yet to make a major impact for club or country so far this season.

Journalist Walid Acherchour made his feelings known on the After Foot programme, saying: 'Zidane hit a wall of reality with this second international break... I found the attitude of some individuals against Turkey to be very poor.

'In the second half against Italy and in the match against Turkey, how do you manage without the ball when you're being torn apart in midfield? Zidane will have to work on all these questions.'.

Acherchour closed by saying bluntly: 'The honeymoon is over.'.

After an ultimately disappointing World Cup in which the French were again by Spain in a major semi-final – following their Euro 2024 exit – long-term manager Didier Deschamps left after 14 years in charge.

Legendary midfielder Zidane succeeded him in the summer and has already led France to the top of their Nations League group – but some of his players may have to go much further to win over their critics.

Noi proponiamo e per il momento tutto sta andando bene. La base di tutto è il lavoro: se vuoi giocare in questo modo qui, la fatica ti deve rimanere nella testa. A parlare è facile, non basta.

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 10:42 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 12:38 EST, 17 November 2026.

Gary Neville has stood up for under-fire Manchester United man Diogo Dalot – and named three of his defensive team-mates he would rather see leave the club before him.

The Portugal international's limp performances have come under heavy scrutiny this season with the decline of Michael Carrick's side as autumn has worn on.

But as Mauricio Pochettino prepares to take over at Old Trafford, Neville urged the new manager not to immediately expel the defender, despite his drop-off in form.

Sources indicate that 'I think if he was in a decent back four he'd be alright,' Neville told Stick to United co-host Mark Goldbridge on Tuesday. 'But he's got a shocking back four alongside him.

It has been revealed that 'Positionally he's not great. He could be better on the ball. He could be better at everything he does. Of course he could. I just think he's such an easy target, Dalot. I honestly do.'.

Neville admitted that sometimes he listens to his fellow Man United-supporting friends deriding Dalot and wonders 'are they watching something that I don't see?'.

Gary Neville has defended Man United star Diogo Dalot - arguing that he has team-mates who are far weaker.

The Portugal international has come in for heavy criticism from supporters this season.

But in his opinion, there are three defenders that he would let go in the 'first wave' of changes in Manchester.

Sources indicate that 'I'd be getting (Noussair) Mazraoui well gone before him,' he continued. 'I'd be getting (Lisandro) Martinez gone well before him. I'll be getting (Matthijs) De Ligt gone well before him.

'(De Ligt has) got one major problem. He doesn’t play football. If a player is injury prone and doesn't play football, just because he hasn't played doesn't mean to say that he should go above a player who's played every single week and he's throwing his hand up. You want someone who's actually reliable and play. De Ligt has to go. De Ligt, Martinez, Mazraoui.'.

Another stalwart in the team that Neville was keen to have a second chance under Pochettino was Luke Shaw.

'He will keep Shaw because he knows him and he'll probably get the best out of him. The problem with Luke is injuries,' he added. 'So he'll have to manage him. So he'll have to bring a left back in. But let's just say who he'll keep.

Sources indicate that 'He'll keep Shaw. He'll keep (Harry) Maguire because he'll trust him and he'll think that he's basically a soldier and someone who can do a job for him.

In a recent development, 'He'll keep (Leny) Yoro because I think he'll think "I've got something there that I can work with". (But) I think he's a little bit gangly, all over the place right now. And he looks like he's going to slip every time. He's got that sort of Bambi-on-ice (look).

According to recent reports, 'Physically what will happen is with Yoro, he'll go one way or the other. I like the fact he's been brought into the French team. It tells me sometimes you just have got to connect the dots and think, "okay, well, if they think he's good, then we must be missing something here because we're not seeing it yet, are we?".'.

Neville went on to suggest that Yoro was lacking the connection within his body that Premier League rivals such as Jeremy Jacquet are already able to harness – something Sir Alex Ferguson had identified in Rio Ferdinand when he was at West Ham.

Like Ferdinand, Neville backed Yoro to flourish as he taps into that connection and improves his strength and stability.

According to recent reports, 'So Yoro he will keep: Yoro, Maguire and Shaw I think he'll keep and I think he'll keep Dalot. To start with,' Neville remarked. 'He'll have to bring in three defenders to go above them. Let's be clear. He'll have to bring in three defenders.

Sources indicate that 'Mazraoui I would lose, De Ligt I would lose because he's injury prone. Martinez 100 per cent. 100 per cent. 100 per cent.'.

As well as struggling for form this season, Martinez has been a challenging presence in the Man United squad this term, boldly calling out the Man United hierarchy during a firebrand interview last month.

Neville was more interested in new head coach Mauricio Pochettino despatching Noussair Mazraoui and Matthijs de Ligt.

Lisandro Martinez has been an unsettled presence in the side this season and hit out at the club's recruiting last month.

The Argentina star implied that he was disappointed with the club's recruitment strategy over the summer, and was forced to hold clear-the-air talks to smooth his return to the side.

Neville added that he would send Ayden Heaven on loan to get experience in the lower divisions to 'build' his ability up, as it was borderline 'unfair' to be 'putting him in' the side at present.

But not all of the changes can come quickly for Pochettino, who has little time before taking charge of Man United against Liverpool at Anfield this weekend.

It has been revealed that 'First wave, end of the season,' Neville clarified of what he believes Pochettino's plan for change will be. 'No, he can't get rid of (them all) in January.

According to recent reports, 'He has to bring one or two defenders in January if he can. But he can't get rid of all those in his first wave. He's only got one month till January.'.

The drawn-out process of sacking Carrick began last week when Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada flew to Monaco for talks with co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer ownership group.

While his future was on the chopping block, Carrick held training sessions at Carrington before the axe finally swung last Thursday.

Pochettino was appointed days later and gave a tearful farewell press conference ahead of his penultimate game with the United States national team on Saturday.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,’ he told the press. ‘It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

In a recent development, ‘When these moments arrive, it is always tough. Normally it is the opposite – you have been sacked! You cry because you want to stay. I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

‘Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

Recent findings suggest that ‘In some part it’s a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'.

Scotland’s ramped-up second-half performance offered some cause for optimism as Sébastien Pocognoli’s tenure as head coach began with a goalless draw with Slovenia in Ljubljana.

The 39-year-old Belgian head coach, appointed in August as Steve Clarke’s successor, refreshed the side for the Nations League Group B1 opener in the Stozice Stadium, but they were fortunate on a couple of occasions at least not to fall behind before rallying before the break.

Scotland had been insipid and uninspiring for most of the first half but after the interval they played with pace and purpose as Slovenia captain and goalkeeper Jan Oblak became a key figure, making saves from Oli McBurnie and Kieron Bowie.

Oli McBurnie spurns a chance for Scotland.It remains goalless between Slovenia and Scotland.📺 Watch on BBC One pic.twitter.com/sldzhNCGGb.

“It took us a bit of getting used to in the first half, the way the gaffer wants to play,” McBurnie told BBC Scotland.

“We created enough chances to win the game. I should have scored. I was asked to play a different position and I enjoyed it. I’d rather be getting in the positions than not getting chances.

Industry observers note that “Second half was a lot more of what the manager wanted from us. It was waves of pressure and the only thing missing was a goal or two.”.

However, the goal that would have made the former Union Saint-Gilloise and Monaco manager’s debut as an international boss more memorable ultimately failed to arrive.

In this extended international break, the Scots will host Switzerland at Hampden on Tuesday and then travel to North Macedonia before taking on Slovenia in Glasgow, with the Tartan Army hoping to see further improvement – and goals.

September 29: Scotland vs Switzerland.

October 3: North Macedonia vs Scotland.

October 6: Scotland vs Slovenia.

November 13: Scotland vs North Macedonia.

November 16: Switzerland vs Scotland.

Speaking to BBC Scotland, the debutant stated: “Thought we struggled to get into the game first half, but second half we completely dominated the game.

Industry observers note that “They’ve got a top goalie who made really good saves. So many positives to take and a clean sheet as well.

“We changed shape a wee bit at half-time to get more control and that did really well for us.

“It’s a big game again on Tuesday so it’s key to recover now and go again.

“I’ve played on the left-hand side for a couple of years now, so I’m comfortable doing that.

According to recent reports, “We’ve had a great week. A latest manager, new way of playing and new faces in camp. It’s just the chances we need to take - the fact we’re creating the chances stands us in good stead.”.

The striker told BBC Scotland: “It took us a bit of getting used to in the first half, the way the gaffer wants to play.

“We created enough chances to win the game. I should have scored.

It has been revealed that “I was asked to play a different position and I enjoyed it. I’d rather be getting in the positions than not getting chances.

Industry observers note that “Second half was a lot more of what the manager wanted from us. It was waves of pressure and the only thing missing was a goal or two.”.

Sources indicate that pocognoli’s first game in charge of Scotland ends in a goalless draw. The visitors produced a dominant second-half display, but their final ball and end-product was severely lacking in crucial moments. Ure, Hickey, Gilmour, McBurnie and Bowie all came close to scoring, but no one could break the deadlock.

Recent findings suggest that scotland cannot find a way past the impenetrable Oblak. There will be just two minutes of added time for the visitors to possibly score a late winner.

It has been revealed that lovric clatters into Gilmour and is cautioned. Slovenia can’t get out. It’s wave after wave of Scottish pressure.

Recent findings suggest that oblak comes out and fails to claim Robertson’s free-kick. The ball is recycled and the Tottenham full-back whips a second cross into the box and Slovenia fail to clear. Welsh is waiting for it, but lashes a first-time volley over the bar.

Karnicnik catches Robertson with a late lunging tackle and receives a yellow card, giving Scotland a chance to get the ball into the box.

The hosts make their fifth alteration of the afternoon, with Cerin withdrawn and Lovric on instead.

How has Bowie missed?! Gilmour finds Bowie with an outstanding pass through the centre of Slovenia’s defence. The substitute takes a touch then scuffs a rushed finish wide. Bowie has to do better there!

Another change is here for Scotland, with Gannon-Doak on to replace Hickey.

Another massive chance for Scotland. This time Sassuolo's Kieron Bowie goes close.Slovenia 0-0 Scotland - watch the closing stages on BBC One. pic.twitter.com/xMe5gRNgEr.

From the resulting corner, Oblak is there again to thwart McBurnie’s point-blank header. The referee then blows his whistle to relieve the pressure on Slovenia. Somehow, the scoreline remains goalless.

The hosts make another double change as Sporar and Brekalo depart for Vipotnik and Balkovec.

Welsh spots Bowie’s run and threads a perfectly-weighted pass through to the forward. From an unfavourable angle, the substitute’s one-on-one attempt is blocked by Oblak.

Sources indicate that another massive chance for Scotland! McGinn’s searching corner is met by Hickey, who flicks a header wide of the far post. Scotland’s second-half performance deserves a goal.

Pocognoli orders Scotland’s first alteration of the game, with Bowie replacing Ure up top.

Hickey finds himself very high up the pitch and tries to tee up Ure with a cushioned header, but there isn’t enough power on the pass.

Gilmour and Ure link up effectively on the counter, but the latter’s pull-back is intercepted by Drkusic.

Slovenia then make two changes as Zabukovnik and Zec replace Elsnik and Drkusic.

According to recent reports, mcGinn strides forward and tries to find Ure, but Slovenia rush back to scramble it clear. Scotland are really pushing for the opening goal.

According to recent reports, gilmour and McBurnie play a devastating one-two, allowing the midfielder to advance into the penalty area. He shoots and aims for the far corner, but his placed effort is collected impressively by Oblak, who makes another crucial intervention.

Recent findings suggest that the second half has started as the first ended, with Scotland applying all of the pressure. Slovenia have Oblak to thank for the goalless scoreline.

McBurnie and Oblak both challenge for the ball, with the Scotsman bumping into the goalkeeper, giving Slovenia a goal kick. The decision is met by a chorus of boos from the away fans.

McBurnie latches onto a loose ball and skips away from Drkusic’s sliding challenge. One-on-one, the striker tries to round Oblak, but the Slovenian goalkeeper does sensationally to apprehend him. Upon reflection, it looks like McBurnie should have just shot and tried to put the ball between Oblak’s legs. He did the hard part, but lacked a clinical finish.

Oli McBurnie spurns a chance for Scotland.It remains goalless between Slovenia and Scotland.📺 Watch on BBC One pic.twitter.com/sldzhNCGGb.

McGinn brilliantly turns Drkusic on the halfway line and then tees up Gilmour. The Napoli midfielder tries to float a pass over to the onrushing Robertson, but he hits the switch of play straight out for a throw-in. In defence of Gilmour, the pitch really doesn’t look in the best condition, with various players struggling regarding their weight of pass.

It has been revealed that we are back under way for the second half. Both sides are unchanged at the break.

Sources indicate that pocognoli’s Scotland finished the half as the better side, but an opening goal has proved to be elusive. At times, they’ve looked suspect defensively and have lacked rhythm going forward. However, Pocognoli’s squad have only been together for a few days and are playing in a new system. Can they produce a more inspired second-half performance?

Despite Scotland’s late push for an opening goal at the end of the first half, the two sides head in level at the break. Slovenia started on the front-foot, with Sporar and Drkusic both going close for the hosts, before Ure struck the post to be denied a dream debut goal.

Sources indicate that ure strikes the woodwork! The Sevilla striker is agonisingly close to a debut goal for his country. He cuts inside to work some space and fires a low effort at goal, but his shot hits the post.

Scotland's best chance of the game so far 😯 Sevilla striker and debutant Robbie Ure strikes the post just before half-time.However, it remains goalless at the break.📺 Watch Slovenia v Scotland on BBC One 🇸🇮 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿 pic.twitter.com/fm1wH2fOej.

In a recent development, much better from Scotland! McGinn turns his marker and clips a wonderful pass over to Ure, who has drifted out wide. The ball is then delivered into the box toward McGinn, whose header bounces off McBurnie. Hickey is arriving to pounce on the loose ball, but the wing-back’s effort is blocked by the Slovenian defence.

Industry observers note that robertson picks up the game’s first yellow card for an off-the-ball incident. The Scotland captain is clearly very unhappy with the decision as we await to see a replay. Nevertheless, the action resumes with a Slovenia free-kick.

Recent findings suggest that slovenia go close again as a corner is whipped in. Drkusic wins the header at the near post and it bounces off the outside of the near post. That is definitely another warning sign for Scotland.

Matko goes on the outside of Welsh, and from a tight angle, he shoots, but his fizzed effort saves the side netting of the near post. Some fans behind the goal cheer because they think it’s gone in, but their view has really deceived them.

Industry observers note that it’s been a quiet afternoon for both goalkeepers so far, with neither yet to make a noteworthy save. On a couple of occasions, Slovenia have had encouraging opportunities to get the ball into the Scotland’s box, but the deliveries have been overhit and poorly executed.

Similarly to Scotland, Slovenia are also playing a tremendously high-line. Unlike Slovenia, Scotland have been unable to find the right pass in behind the home side’s defence. Gilmour then carelessly gives the ball away as Scotland’s latest spell of possession ends.

Recent findings suggest that since Slovenia wasted that 14th-minute chance, Scotland have grown into the contest and are beginning to look comfortable in possession. However, they’re still waiting to craft their first notable opening here.

Sources indicate that the hosts miss a huge chance! Once again, Sturm gets in behind Scotland’s incredibly high line and then fires a low cross into the penalty area. Sporar then beats McKenna to the delivery, but taps his close-range effort wide of the far post from inside the six-yard box. That’s a massive let-off for Scotland...

Recent findings suggest that matko is unleashed by a drilled pass then pierces through a gap between Robertson and Welsh. The Slovenia winger drives into the penalty area and tries to find either Sturm or Sporar with a cross, but Hendry does magnificently to make a last-ditch clearance.

Slovenia have the ball in the net, but the offside flag is up. Sturm gets in behind Scotland’s defence and slides a low cross into Sporar’s path. The striker then sweeps a composed first-time effort into the top corner. It’s a brilliant finish, but Sturm was miles offside in the build-up.

Gunn comes out confidently to collect a looping cross, before the ball is introduced forward in McBurnie’s direction. The Hull City striker and Ure are playing really close to each other, very much like an old-school front-two.

Sources indicate that slovenia forward Sturm is wiped out by Hendry’s wild early challenge. The Scotland defender is perhaps lucky to avoid a booking. Welsh then heads the resulting set-piece away and out for a corner.

According to recent reports, the hosts get us underway in the Slovenian capital. Can Pocognoli begin his Scotland tenure with a Nations League victory?

In a recent development, both teams are out on the pitch in Ljubljana. We are moments away from the start of the Pocognoli era.

Subs: Kelly, Bain, Binks, Doig, Christie, Miller, McPake, Doak, Graham, Bowie, Patterson, Montgomery.

On paper, it looks like Sebastien Pocognoli has opted for a five-back formation, with Swansea City defender Stephen Welsh making his Scotland debut as one of the centre backs.

Captain Andy Robertson and Brentford’s Aaron Hickey will operate as the wing-backs, with Billy Gilmour, Lewis Ferguson and John McGinn forming a midfield three.

A upcoming-look attack is spearheaded by the returning Oli McBurnie and 22-year-old Robbie Ure, who like Welsh, will also make his Scotland debut.

Angus Gunn remains his country’s first-choice goalkeeper.

“The first game is always a special game so you have to bring the mental aspect in for the players and for the staff.

Sources indicate that “We need to create a good energy but it’s up to us on the pitch to create this. So then we can be hand in hand with the supporters.”.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this UEFA Nations League B, Group 1 match as Slovenia host Scotland at Stozice Stadium in Ljubljana.

Scotland qualified for their first World Cup in 28 years this summer, but they exited the tournament with a whimper after failing to finish as one of the best third-place group sides. Steve Clarke’s men beat tournament debutants Haiti 1-0 in their opening match, before falling to defeats without scoring against Morocco and Brazil.

Following the World Cup, Clarke stepped down as Scotland’s head coach, ending a seven-year tenure, and was replaced by Belgian manager Sebastien Pocognoli. The former Monaco boss will take charge of his first game in his fresh role today and will be itching to make an encouraging start in a new era for Scottish football.

Over this extended international break, Pocognoli’s side will also face Switzerland and North Macedonia, as well as a return fixture against Slovenia in Scotland on October 6 to round off a busy period.

While Scotland took part in the World Cup, Slovenia were reflecting on their hugely disappointing qualification performance, where they finished third in their group behind Switzerland and Kosovo without winning and netting just three goals across six matches.

Manchester United striker Benjamin Sesko – Slovenia’s star man and most well-known player – withdrew from Bostjan Cesar’s squad earlier this week after the recurrence of a shin injury caused the 23-year-old to completely miss the 1-1 draw against Fulham last Sunday.

Scotland have a few notable absences, with Scott McTominay, Che Adams and Lawrence Shankland all unavailable, but Billy Gilmour returns to the fold after missing the World Cup through injury, Oli McBurnie has been recalled and Sevilla striker Robbie Ure has received his first senior call-up.

Kick-off is at 14:00, with team news coming shortly.

#49841. The curious case of Sebastien Pocognoli looks certain to have a grisly ending... the SFA have hired a dud

The curious case of Sebastien Pocognoli looks certain to have a grisly ending... the SFA have hired a dud

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1396 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.
  • Published: 14:13 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 14:26 EST, 17 November 2026.
  • Of all the many stories written by F Scott Fitzgerald, one of the finest authors and wordsmiths of his time, The Great Gatsby will forever remain his masterpiece.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 14:13 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 14:26 EST, 17 November 2026.

Of all the many stories written by F Scott Fitzgerald, one of the finest authors and wordsmiths of his time, The Great Gatsby will forever remain his masterpiece.

In some of his other work written as he travelled across Europe, Fitzgerald also had a line about Switzerland, describing it as a ‘country where very few things begin, but many things end.’.

It is a curious quote and, like much of Fitzgerald’s work, is open to interpretation. As the man who also wrote The Curious Case of Benjamin Button, curiosity was a common theme.

As for the Curious Case of Sebastien Pocognoli, Switzerland may, indeed, be the country where everything came to an end.

Sources indicate that what unfolded in St Gallen on Monday evening was a horror show. Scotland were battered 4-0 by Switzerland’s B team. There is no way to sugar-coat a result like that, no way to dress it up as anything other than an embarrassment. They played OK for half an hour and then fell apart.

Pocognoli claimed afterwards that there were positives to be taken and how some of Scotland’s football was the best they have produced across his six matches in charge.

Sebastien Pocognoli is facing serious questions after a miserable Nations League campaign.

It has been revealed that utter nonsense. That was a manager clutching at straws at the end of a Nations League campaign which has been an unmitigated disaster pretty much from start to finish.

It has been revealed that let’s go back to the very start here. After Steve Clarke had pushed the Scottish Football Association (SFA) into awarding him a latest four-year contract, only to then walk away after the World Cup, it was a chance for a fresh start.

On the day when Pocognoli was unveiled as the fresh head coach in August, Ian Maxwell and Craig Mulholland, the SFA’s chief executive and chief football officer, were beaming with positivity.

They told us all how data and AI had been used in the recruitment process, and how several clubs across Europe had been chasing Pocognoli.

They clearly viewed it as a coup to have landed the 39-year-old Belgian, who had won a league title in his homeland with Union Saint-Gilloise before a short stint with Monaco.

What would the data say now? Six games played, two wins, a draw and three defeats, five goals scored and ten conceded, seven points and a lousy third-placed finish in Group B1.

Both of those wins came against a North Macedonian side who lost all six of their games. They were a pub team – and Scotland still struggled to beat them at Hampden last Friday night.

Pocognoli was unable to inspire any resistance as his side succumbed to defeat in St Gallen.

Scotland lost 7-0 on aggregate to Switzerland over the two games. Against Slovenia, a 0-0 draw on the opening day in Ljubljana was then followed with a woeful 2-1 defeat at Hampden.

Sources indicate that all of which begs a very simple question. Where, exactly, are the grounds for optimism here? How is this getting any better?

When Pocognoli arrived, he spoke about trying to change the style of play, get Scotland playing a more exciting brand of football, whilst bringing through a new generation of players.

It was not a rebuild. He inherited a group of players who were accustomed to success under Clarke and who qualified for three tournaments out of a possible four.

According to recent reports, his remit was to help Scotland take the next step in major tournaments. With a more dynamic style of play, the job was to help the nation take the next step.

There has been no revolution thus far. No evidence whatsoever that this coach is capable of delivering results nor a better style of play.

Industry observers note that there is no satisfaction to be taken in any of this. When Pocognoli was appointed, it was, in the eyes of this observer, an interesting and progressive move.

SFA chiefs Craig Mulholland and Ian Maxwell proudly unveil latest boss Pocognoli at Hampden.

Over the past 48 hours or so, there has been a lot of revisionism from some folk about Clarke. ‘Aye, the grass isn’t always greener...’.

Sources indicate that that’s garbage. Clarke’s time was up with Scotland. He should never have been handed a new four-year deal in the first place. At least he did the right thing in resigning after the World Cup.

The whole thing was finished. The problem is that the SFA look like they have appointed a total dud as his successor. Both of those things can be true at the same time.

It is also worth remembering that the only reason we arrived at Pocognoli is because Clarke walked away. The SFA did not instigate any change.

The hiring of a fresh head coach was not a proactive change of direction, but a reactive move from an executive body who became accepting of Clarke’s limitations and allowed him to position them over a barrel.

Industry observers note that listen, there is nothing inherently wrong with using data and metrics in football. It’s the modern way. Using data to inform decisions and recruitment processes is smart business.

In a recent development, but the data in itself is no guarantee of success. There are some intangibles in football, things which are harder to quantify. Like a manager who blindly sticks to a system which is patently ill-suited to the players at his disposal.

Things like leadership and communication skills. We can cut Pocognoli some slack in that English is not his first language. He comes across as a thoroughly decent and likeable chap. He’s doing his best. He wants to embrace the culture and makes an effort to sing the National Anthem.

Scotland's defeat arose from individual mistakes, a common theme during the Belgian's reign.

In a recent development, all of that is undoubtedly to be welcomed. Good on him. But would anyone describe him as an inspirational figure?

When you listen to him speak, have you ever felt slightly confused in terms of the message he’s actually trying to get across?

Sources indicate that how must that sound in the dressing room? When Andy Robertson spoke post-match on Monday night, there was frustration in his voice.

The captain insisted there is simply no time or patience with these things. Scotland need to deliver results now.

To be fair, there actually would be a degree of patience shown by the Tartan Army towards Pocognoli if there was something to actually believe in.

There was a lot of goodwill towards him at the start. If there were signs across these last six games that he could deliver a more exciting team to watch, they would show patience.

Recent findings suggest that but on the basis of what we’ve seen so far, there’s been absolutely nothing to suggest he can move this team forward. Ask yourself a very simple question – do Scotland pass the eye test?

Are we seeing a team who are playing on the front foot and creating chances? The answer, obviously, is no.

Steve Clarke celebrates Scotland's win over Denmark a year ago... how fans miss such highs.

Many Scotland fans are now confronting the possibility that we might not even qualify for Euro 2028, a tournament which we are co-hosting.

By finishing third in the Nations League, we will now be in pot three for the Euro qualifiers and will face a more difficult group.

Beyond that, we would be relying on the back-door method of one of the best-placed home nations not to qualify directly.

Those Euro qualifiers will start in March of next year. Does Pocognoli even make it that far? Or should the SFA hold their hands up, admit they’ve made a mistake, and rectify it?

That feels unlikely. But on the basis of what we have seen over these first six games, it’s hard to see how this gets any better.

We are worse now than we were at the end under Clarke. Much, much worse. This is not teething problems. It’s a team who have regressed massively under a head coach who was supposed to move the whole thing forward.

Roma Capitale. Ci stiamo avviando a un derby incredibile. Un derby con vista scudetto. Il 13 dicembre ci sarà da divertirci. Dopo la sosta per la Nazionale, l'ultima di questo 2026, il campionato regala un sabato nel segno di Roma. Con due squadre che avevano iniziato la stagione con obiettivi diversi e che ora si ritrovano a duellare sullo stesso palcoscenico. Pochi mesi fa la Lazio era un'area terremotata. Rottura totale tra tifosi e il presidente Lotito, mercato bloccato da una crisi economica soffocante e per rendere la situazione ancora più bollente una clamorosa eliminazione al primo turno di Coppa Italia contro un'avversaria di categoria inferiore. Gattuso, il nuovo allenatore della squadra biancoceleste, poteva finire schiacciato da tutte queste criticità. Invece, probabilmente, proprio nel momento più delicato è nata una magia. Una di quelle che rendono il calcio speciale. Oggi, dopo aver battuto all'Olimpico il Lecce, la Lazio è in testa alla classifica. La squadra biancoceleste può vincere lo scudetto? Sì, può provarci. Non è la formazione più forte del campionato e, di sicuro, non è la favorita. Ma ci sono alcuni buoni motivi per immaginare la Lazio in corsa per il titolo: 1) Gattuso ha costruito un gruppo fantastico; 2) in rosa ci sono giocatori di qualità in ogni reparto; 3) Noslin cresce in maniera impressionante; 4) non fare le Coppe regala punti di vantaggio ai biancocelesti e 5) come ha detto un ex grande del calcio italiano come Sebino Nela (tra l'altro ha vinto uno scudetto con la Roma...) questa Lazio ricorda lo scudettato Verona di Bagnoli.

According to recent reports, anche la Roma può vincere il titolo. In questo caso non si può parlare di sorpresa. La squadra giallorossa era tra le favorite per lo scudetto fin dall'inizio del torneo. Contro il Parma è arrivata un'altra testimonianza della forza di questa Roma. Una macchina da gol. Anche per i giallorossi ci sono alcuni buoni motivi per vederla con il tricolore cucito sul petto: 1) Malen sembra il Batistuta protagonista dell'ultimo scudetto della Roma; 2) Gasperini è un fattore con il suo calcio e le sue idee; 3) Dybala e Soule, stavolta proposti a staffetta, sono una coppia micidiale; 4) la Roma nel 2027 festeggerà il Centenario un motivo in più per centrare un grande risultato e 5) la famiglia Friedkin è pronta a garantire altri due rinforzi nel mercato invernale.

In a recent development, È stato anche un grande sabato per il Como. Mister Fabregas è riuscito a voltare pagina dopo la batosta rimediata contro l'Inter prima dello stop e dopo le cattive notizie sulle condizioni fisiche di Kean. Un investimento da quaranta milioni che non ha dato frutti e non li darà per altri mesi. Il Como però ha trovato un suo equilibrio, sa gestire i momenti delle partite, sa andare oltre i momenti di difficoltà. E ha un giocatore speciale come Ramon capace di segnare un gol fondamentale e di evitarne uno con un incredibile recupero difensivo. Normale che sia nel mirino del Real Madrid. Ma intanto se lo gode il Como. E questo Como ha tutto per essere la mina vagante del campionato. Con tutte le carte in regola per riconquistare un posto nella prossima Champions.

It has been revealed that chiudiamo con il Napoli. La vittoria sul Torino allontana i problemi. Anche se la squadra di Allegri resta malaticcia. Un aspetto però emerge chiaro: De Laurentiis deve fare di tutto per allungare prima possibile il contratto a McTominay. È lui la figura intorno alla quale ricostruire un progetto vincente. Dopo aver risolto i suoi problemi di salute sta segnando a raffica. Se il Napoli è ancora vivo e se Allegri è ancora sulla panchina partenopea è tutto merito suo.

Man United Confidential: Mauricio Pochettino to be given money to spend in January as club target recruits in THREE positions - and surprise at popular coach's sacking

  • Mauricio Pochettino’s whirlwind arrival as Manchester United’s new head coach has left little time to work out where he will live – but a key factor in that decision will be his beloved dog Sansa.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:00 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 15:04 EST, 17 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino’s whirlwind arrival as Manchester United’s new head coach has left little time to work out where he will live – but a key factor in that decision will be his beloved dog Sansa.

Pochettino will leave the TQL Stadium in Cincinnati after the USA’s game against Haiti in the early hours of Wednesday morning and go straight to the airport to catch an eight-hour flight to Manchester on board a private jet paid for by United.

The club will also provide him with somewhere to live as he settles into the new job and finds a more permanent residence.

The 54-year-old, who also has a home in Barcelona, is said to have lived just outside London when he was Tottenham manager and then spent the entirety of his 18-month spell as Paris Saint-Germain boss in a luxury hotel.

Pochettino lived in Knightsbridge while he was in charge of Chelsea, and revealed that he enjoyed getting feedback from fans while out on his daily 90-minute dog walks with Sansa.

He named the Rhodesian Ridgeback after a character from Game of Thrones and has even given the dog her own Instagram account.

Mauricio Pochettino will take charge of the US national team for the final time in the early hours of Wednesday morning, then head straight to Manchester on a private jet.

Pochettino (pictured with his son Maurizio) will have to find accommodation which suits his dog Sansa, a Rhodesian Ridgeback (Source: Instagram/pochettino).

Describing the difficulty of Spurs playing on a Saturday night in 2018, he said: ‘At 7pm, I am normally on my sofa with my dog Sansa watching the Spanish league because they start at 7.45pm, or France because Ligue 1 starts at 8pm, or Italy, or different games.

‘It will be so strange for my dog. Not for me but my dog. “Where is my dad?” she is going to say. She is beautiful and I am in love with her.’.

According to recent reports, the living habits of United bosses have varied over the years. Sir Alex Ferguson, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and Ruben Amorim favoured Wilmslow and Alderley Edge, David Moyes remained further afield in Lytham, Louis van Gaal and Erik ten Hag chose Hale, and Jose Mourinho famously spent 895 days at the Lowry Hotel in Manchester (where dogs can stay for an additional £30).

United have no plans to change the timings for Wednesday’s training session, even though Pochettino and four of his backroom team may not arrive at Carrington until the early afternoon.

The private jet carrying the Argentine, first-team coach Miguel D’Agostino, strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya and analyst Alec Scott should touch down from Cincinnati around noon.

An advance party of three more coaches – Pochettino’s assistant Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez, and his son and fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino – have been in Manchester since Sunday after they were released early by the US Soccer Federation as a gesture of goodwill following the 6-0 first-leg win over Haiti in the quarter-finals of the North American equivalent of the Nations League.

They took training on Tuesday as United’s players continue to report back from international duty, and will also oversee the session on Wednesday morning after United decided not to reschedule it so Pochettino could be present.

The Argentine will be firmly hands-on from Thursday, though, as he prepares for his first game against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

Pochettino, who will speak to club media shortly after his arrival before conducting his first press conference on Friday, has faced Liverpool 19 times in his managerial career, losing 11 games, drawing five and winning three.

Pochettino's assistant Jesus Perez (right) has been in Manchester since Sunday and took training on Tuesday.

Strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya - the first woman to be part of United's backroom staff - will travel with Pochettino to Manchester following the Haiti game.

Pochettino will inherit a team in the relegation zone – which could even be bottom of the Premier League by kick-off on Sunday – and it’s understood he will be given modest funds to improve his squad in the January transfer window.

United are in desperate need of a left back and a striker, having failed to sign cover in both positions in the summer.

According to recent reports, one potential target may be US centre forward Folarin Balogun who has prospered under Pochettino but only started once for Monaco this season after a summer move to Everton fell through. United sources say the fresh head coach will have input in the weeks ahead before a clearer initiative emerges.

United also want a centre back after Confidential revealed last week that Fulham’s Calvin Bassey and Nathan Collins, of Brentford, are two options being considered.

It’s possible that one of those deals may have to be a loan, however, with United’s delicate financial situation set to be spelt out in black and white when the results from the first quarter of the financial year are released on Thursday.

Although Pochettino is going to have money for newly introduced players, United will have to be smart in their transfer dealings and spend wisely.

In the short term, Luke Shaw and Marcus Rashford may be available again for the first time in more than a month against Liverpool.

However, there is a concern over Patrick Dorgu who was deemed to be unfit for international duty with Denmark, even though he returned to action for Michael Carrick’s final game after a month-and-a-half out with a hamstring injury and headed a stoppage-time equaliser in the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa.

Fulham's Calvin Bassey (right) is among the centre-back options United are considering.

Marcus Rashford may be available for the first time in more than a month against Liverpool.

It was the departure of Travis Binnion, rather than Carrick, that raised the most eyebrows among figures working in football over the past few days.

Agents and first-team players privately described their surprise at seeing Binnion – a long-time academy figure before stepping up to the first team to help Darren Fletcher as interim and then Carrick – leave the club.

United have cleaned house for the arrival of Pochettino’s backroom team, and Binnion was one of those who paid the price.

A popular figure in the dressing room, Joshua Zirkzee, Benjamin Sesko and Kobbie Mainoo are among the players who are known to have enjoyed working with Binnion.

Despite stepping up to the first team, where he would watch matches from the press box alongside United’s team of analysts, Binnion remained in contact with numerous academy player representatives to ensure their development was progressing as planned.

Binnion, who first arrived in 2019 as an Under 16s coach and progressed to the Under 18s, Under 21s and then head of player development and coaching, isn’t expected to be out of the game for too long though.

Agency sources believe rival Premier League academies will move promptly to recruit him, with Everton seen as one potential landing spot. United’s former academy head Nick Cox is now Everton technical director and has already recruited Dave Hughes and Tom Curtis, who worked under Binnion at United.

A popular figure in the dressing room, Joshua Zirkzee, Benjamin Sesko and Kobbie Mainoo are among the players who enjoyed working with Travis Binnion (pictured).

Your responses to our 36-man Manchester United squad audit have made for interesting reading over the last week.

Confidential pored over the first-team squad, as well as numerous rising stars in the academy, that Pochettino and his staff will quickly have to run the rule over.

While some of the voting went as expected – your votes demonstrated an overwhelming desire among the fanbase to see Noussair Mazraoui, Diogo Dalot, Shaw and Harry Maguire leave this summer – there were a few surprises.

In a recent development, many voted for captain Bruno Fernandes, who just recently rejected a second contract extension offer, to be moved on, along with Rashford. Amad Diallo and summer signing Andrey Santos are two who divide opinion, but both made the cut.

Check out the full squad audit HERE to see how others voted and leave your own verdict!

Confidential understands JJ Gabriel’s representatives held fresh talks with Real Madrid at the club’s training ground on Monday as a move to the Santiago Bernabeu edges ever closer.

Now that Gabriel has officially confirmed a partnership with Epic Sports Agency, his agent Ali Barat is leading negotiations and has been at Real’s Valdebebas headquarters along with the 16-year-old and his family.

Gabriel announced his departure from the club in an Instagram video on Tuesday night, as he and the Spanish giants hope to get a move over the line.

JJ Gabriel's representatives have held fresh talks with Real Madrid as his move to the Bernabeu edges closer.

Eric Cantona and Sir Alex Ferguson will reunite next month at a special screening of the Frenchman’s newly introduced documentary.

Cantona: Flower of Evil won rave reviews in France and is now heading to the UK, with a one-night-only panel featuring Cantona and Ferguson at Aviva Studios in Manchester on December 7.

It has been revealed that the documentary film digs deeper into how Ferguson channelled Cantona’s brilliance and honed his explosiveness – a trait that had seen him branded ‘unmanageable’ in France. Tickets range from £156 all the way up to £1,000. You can purchase them here.
